_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.register: neutral, works across MSA and all regions
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the umbrella term for the whole site's core function; it is the natural term, not a stiff translation of 'fancy font'.
phrases.good_example: زخرفة اسماء ونصوص — اكتب اسمك وزخرفه (ar/zakhrafa H1)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a — this is the correct primary term

phrases.register: neutral, MSA, matches actual search queries
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary keyword for the ar/zakhrafa hub; matches native forum search behavior exactly.
phrases.good_example: أداة زخرفة اسماء ونصوص مجانية (ar/zakhrafa meta description)

phrases.content_surface: titles, meta descriptions, CTAs, FAQ how-to steps
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in titles/meta as the trust signal ('free, copy-paste, no app').
phrases.good_example: خط للبايو — زخرفة نصوص بايو انستقرام (نسخ ولصق مجاناً) (ar/usecase/khat-bio title)

phrases.content_surface: library hub pages, zakhrafa tool tabs
phrases.usage_guidance: Core taxonomy term for the whole library/symbol section (51 files reference it).
phrases.good_example: الرموز والأحرف الخاصة — رموز للنسخ (نجوم، قلوب، زخارف) (ar/library/special-characters title)

phrases.usage_guidance: Use specifically for symbols that wrap a name on both sides (as opposed to رموز, the broader symbol category).
phrases.good_example: إطارات الأسماء ꧁꧂ (ar/zakhrafa H2)

phrases.register: MSA, technically precise, genuinely Arabic-native (not a Latin-script decoration concept)
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the single most important Arabic-native (not translated) decoration mechanic on the site — use it prominently whenever addressing 'does decoration work with Arabic names'.
phrases.good_example: أقدم زخرفة عربية وأكثرها أماناً: حرف المدّ «ـ» (التطويل) يمدّ الوصلة بين الحروف المتصلة فيتحول «محمد» إلى «محـمـد» (ar/zakhrafa)

phrases.usage_guidance: Pair with الكشيدة as the second Arabic-native decoration technique.
phrases.good_example: وللمزيد من الأناقة أضف التشكيل: «مُحَمَّدٌ» — فالحركات تُقرأ زينةً وتوثيقاً للنطق في آن واحد (ar/zakhrafa)

phrases.content_surface: answers/ism-mustakhdim-am-ism-zahir (whole page built around this distinction)
phrases.usage_guidance: Always contrast explicitly with الاسم الظاهر — this is the site's core 'where does decoration actually work' explainer.
phrases.good_example: أين تعمل الخطوط المزخرفة — اسم المستخدم أم الاسم الظاهر؟ (page title)

phrases.usage_guidance: The correct target field to recommend decoration for; keep paired with the اسم المستخدم contrast.
phrases.good_example: الاسم الظاهر تسمية، فيقبل يونيكود المزخرف. ضع الزخرفة في حقل الاسم الظاهر واترك اسم المستخدم بسيطاً.

phrases.register: MSA, formal — notably NOT the borrowed 'نك/نكنيم' slang the prior forum research flagged
phrases.usage_guidance: The repo consistently prefers this formal MSA term over the borrowed slang 'نك/نكنيم' that ar-existing.json's forum research found in Gulf/Levant gaming forums. This is a deliberate register choice fitting the pan-Arabic default.
phrases.good_example: زخرف حقل الاسم/اللقب والنبذة بدلاً من ذلك (ar/answers/ism-mustakhdim-am-ism-zahir)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a on the pan-Arabic site; a Gulf-targeted gaming-forum-style page could reasonably use نك/نكنيم instead

phrases.register: colloquial/social, but standard across the Arabic internet, used as the primary search term
phrases.usage_guidance: Used in titles/H1 where it matches actual search behavior (خط للبايو); body copy tends to gloss it with the more formal النبذة. This split appears intentional, not accidental — keep it.
phrases.good_example: خط للبايو — زخرفة نصوص بايو انستقرام (نسخ ولصق مجاناً) (ar/usecase/khat-bio title)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a — appropriate as the primary keyword term

phrases.usage_guidance: Correctly paired with 'علامات استفهام' (question marks) as the two failure symptoms of the same missing-glyph problem.
phrases.good_example: لماذا يظهر اسمي كمربعات أو علامات استفهام؟ (answers page title)

phrases.register: neutral MSA, matches actual in-app/game error strings
phrases.usage_guidance: Reuse the exact error-message phrasing verbatim — this is what users search for when troubleshooting.
phrases.good_example: تلصق اسماً مزخرفاً، فيُرفض برسالة «أحرف غير صالحة» (ar/answers/ism-mustakhdim-am-ism-zahir)

phrases.usage_guidance: Pair with the caveat that support varies by app/game and some games treat blank names as a rule violation.
phrases.good_example: كيفية إنشاء اسم فارغ (غير مرئي) (page title)

phrases.english_concept: invisible character (Unicode trick used for blank names/fake spacing)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for the 'add a space inside my game name' job specifically, distinct from اسم فارغ (fully blank name).
phrases.good_example: مسافة في اسم فري فاير؟ استخدم الحرف غير المرئي (ar/usecase/asmaa-free-fire H2)

phrases.english_concept: rename card (in-game currency item to change your name)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the 'don't waste it' loss-aversion hook — matches the site's live-checker value proposition (check length before spending the card).
phrases.good_example: لا تُهدر بطاقة تغيير اسم (answers/sabab-rafd-ism-allaeba H2)

phrases.register: borrowed-word gaming register, standard across the region
phrases.usage_guidance: Pair with وسم قصير (تاغ) — clan name + short tag every member prefixes their name with.
phrases.good_example: اسماء كلانات وقروبات فري فاير (H2)

phrases.english_concept: clan tag (short prefix every team member puts on their name)
phrases.register: MSA term (وسم) glossed with the borrowed English loanword (تاغ) in parentheses — a deliberate bilingual-gloss pattern
phrases.usage_guidance: Keep the bilingual gloss pattern (formal Arabic term + borrowed English in parentheses) — it hedges against readers who only know the English gaming term 'tag'.
phrases.good_example: ومعه وسم قصير (تاغ) يضعه كل عضو في بداية اسمه ليعرف الجميع فريقكم في اللوبي (ar/usecase/asmaa-free-fire)

phrases.english_concept: gamer symbols (ツ 彡 メ 〆 亗 ☠ ⚔)
phrases.country_or_market: pan-Arab, gaming (matches global gamer-symbol conventions, not Arabic-specific)
phrases.usage_guidance: Individual glyph labels (e.g. 'ذيل السرعة' for 彡, 'علامة القنص' for 〆) are creative but natural MSA glosses, not literal translations of the Japanese-origin meanings — good craft.
phrases.good_example: الرموز الأكثر انتشاراً في أسماء ببجي وفري فاير حول العالم (ar/zakhrafa)

phrases.english_concept: Arabic-script ornaments and Islamic symbols used in decoration
phrases.country_or_market: pan-Arab / religious-cultural, cuts across all regions
phrases.usage_guidance: IMPORTANT: the repo explicitly excludes ﷽ (Basmala) from the decoration set with an on-page caution note — do not treat all Islamic-symbol glyphs as decoration-safe by default.
phrases.good_example: ملاحظة: رمز البسملة ﷽ رمز ديني وليس زخرفة — نرجو عدم استخدامه في الأسماء (ar/zakhrafa)
phrases.avoid_when: Do not list ﷽ or similarly sacred phrases (ﷺ) as decorative name symbols — repo already self-corrects for this

phrases.register: colloquial-leaning (بايو) matched with formal head noun (خط)
phrases.usage_guidance: Good example of matching real search phrasing rather than a stiffer MSA equivalent like 'خط للنبذة الشخصية'.
phrases.good_example: خط للبايو (page H1)

phrases.usage_guidance: The FAQ explicitly notes this also works with Arabic script, an important cross-script confirmation for RTL users.
phrases.good_example: يعمل مع العربية واللاتينية، ويوفّر أكثر من 12 تخطيطاً (locales/ar.json FAQ)

phrases.country_or_market: Gulf-leaning (explicit Gulf-identity naming found), broadly pan-Arab gaming
phrases.usage_guidance: Candidate 'style name' vocabulary for future ready-made-name copy on Free Fire/PUBG usecase pages, alongside اسم مرعب (scary).
phrases.good_example: اسماء فري فاير مزخرفة 2026 — 100+ اسم فخم جاهز للنسخ (شباب وبنات) (zakhrafah.net title)

phrases.usage_guidance: One of the two dominant Free-Fire naming aesthetics found in the wild (the other being فخم/fancy) — the site's current ready-made names (ar/usecase/asmaa-free-fire) lean fancy/warrior (⚔ 💀 already present) but do not explicitly label a 'مرعب' category.
phrases.good_example: زخرفة اسماء فري فاير عربي — زخرفة إسم المرعب فري فاير عربي (free-fire.ru.ma page title)

phrases.english_concept: romantic-address decorated names ('name for my beloved')
phrases.usage_guidance: Distinct use case from gaming or bio decoration — decorating a saved contact name/pet name for a partner. Not currently served by any UltraTextGen usecase page.
phrases.good_example: قائمة أسماء للحبيب للواتس مزخرفة +300 أسماء للحبيب للواتس مزخرفة (mr7baksa.com page title)

phrases.english_concept: offensive/policy-violating words (a different rejection reason than character-set rejection)
phrases.usage_guidance: The repo's existing rejection-troubleshooting content (answers/sabab-rafd-ism-allaeba, zuhoor-alism-murabbaat) is entirely about character-set/glyph-support rejection. This is a genuinely different rejection cause (content moderation) that none of the current answers/ pages address — worth flagging as a scope gap rather than conflating with the existing char-set FAQ.
phrases.good_example: يجب التأكد من أن الاسم لا يحتوي على كلمات مسيئة أو مخالفة لسياسات تيك توك (sqorebda3.com/vb/threads/87299/, directly fetched)

phrases.usage_guidance: Naming a decorated Snapchat Private Story is a distinct, real search cluster ('اسماء برايفت ستوري سناب') not currently served by ar/khat-snapchat, which covers general Snapchat fonts but not this specific named-feature naming job.
phrases.good_example: اسماء برايفت ستوري سناب بالعربي .. عاطفية ومميزة (almrsal.com title)

phrases.usage_guidance: Standard enough to use as an alternate gloss for 'profile' contexts, though the repo currently prefers formal المستخدم/الحساب framing instead.
phrases.good_example: بروفايل — يشير المصطلح إلى ملف المستخدم الشخصي على تطبيقات التواصل الاجتماعي (search summary, almrsal.com)

phrases.english_concept: Gulf regional identity as a naming theme
phrases.usage_guidance: The clearest single piece of evidence in this research run that regional (not just pan-Arabic) identity is an active naming motif — the pan-Arabic /ar/ page should keep this as an example/note, not the main term, per the task's regional-handling instruction.
phrases.good_example: أمير العرب (Arab Prince) / ملك الخليج (Gulf King) / ابن الخليج (Gulf Son) (zakhrafah.net, directly fetched, gender/region-differentiated name list)
phrases.avoid_when: on the pan-Arabic default page's primary term — fine as a regional example in a Free Fire ready-made-names list

phrases.english_concept: Arabic letters rendering disconnected / separated / reversed when a tool does not shape Arabic (the breakage users describe)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use verbatim as an Arabic FAQ heading wherever the site offers a per-character transform (curved text, vertical/stacked text, styled Unicode fonts): 'لماذا تظهر الحروف متقطعة ومنفصلة؟'. This is the honest answer surface for why Arabic input degrades in these features — Arabic is cursive and joins depend on neighbours, so any per-glyph operation breaks the word. Answering this well is a genuine differentiator against machine-translated competitors, which simply do not mention it.
phrases.good_example: لماذا تظهر الحروف متقطعة ومنفصلة عند تحويل النص؟ لأن الحروف العربية تتصل ببعضها، وأي تنسيق يتعامل مع كل حرف على حدة يفصلها.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use for missing-glyph/tofu rendering (that is a different failure — see AR-013 for the rejected-character sense). Do not use in marketing copy; it belongs in FAQ/help register only.

phrases.english_concept: kaomoji / Japanese-style text face — and the absence of a settled Arabic term
phrases.country_or_market: pan-Arab MSA (not dialect-specific; Gulf vs Egypt not distinguished)
phrases.content_surface: body copy, faq, category headings — the H1 should lean on AR-004 'رموز' phrasing plus the visual examples
phrases.usage_guidance: An Arabic kaomoji page cannot assume the word. Lead with the familiar 'رموز' framing plus a visible example string, and introduce 'كاوموجي' as the name of the thing, glossed as 'الرموز اليابانية'. Because the vocabulary is unsettled, the SHOWN EXAMPLE does more targeting work than the noun does — put real faces in the H1/hero.
phrases.good_example: رموز يابانية ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) للنسخ واللصق — تُعرف باسم «كاوموجي»، وهي وجوه مصنوعة من الحروف والرموز فقط.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'كاوموجي' bare with no gloss — most Arabic readers will not recognise it. Do not carry Gulf-specific gaming register into MSA explanatory copy (see AR-033 for the Gulf-identity boundary already recorded).

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'فن أسكي' with the Latin 'ASCII art' beside it — Arabic technical searchers very commonly type the Latin string even in an otherwise Arabic query, so carrying both in the title covers the split without keyword-stuffing.
phrases.good_example: فن أسكي (ASCII art): صور مصنوعة بالكامل من حروف ورموز لوحة المفاتيح، جاهزة للنسخ.
phrases.avoid_when: Don't use it for single face emoticons. Avoid in casual social-media copy where nobody names the technique.

phrases.english_concept: Diwani script — the specific Arabic script chosen for wedding invitations and formal decrees
phrases.country_or_market: pan-Arab (evidence from a professional calligraphy service and Saudi/Gulf invitation shops; not verified for Maghreb usage)
phrases.usage_guidance: Name the specific script when the copy is about a ceremonial Arabic-script piece — it is the difference between sounding informed and sounding machine-translated. Note this site's Arabic output is Latin-script Unicode styling plus زخرفة (AR-001); it cannot render Diwani, so any mention must be explanatory, never a product claim.
phrases.good_example: الخط الديواني يمنح دعوة الزفاف حضورًا راقيًا، خاصة في الحفلات التقليدية.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages. Never present a Unicode style as الخط الديواني — it is a real calligraphic script and the claim would be false. And keep زخرفة (AR-001), the site's own head term, out of ceremonial copy: زخرفة connotes the gaming/name-decoration tool category and would cheapen a wedding-stationery page instantly.

phrases.english_concept: the couple, as named on a wedding invitation
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the label for a ceremonial name example. The dual form is the marker of native copy — 'اسم العروس والعريس' is correct but reads as unpacked-from-English.
phrases.good_example: يُكتب اسم العروسين بخط فني في وسط البطاقة، والتفاصيل بخط بسيط.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages — the site's Arabic gaming vocabulary is اسم المستخدم / اللقب / نك نيم (AR-008/AR-010/AR-023) and this belongs to a different reader entirely. Note also AR-027 (اسماء للحبيب) is the romantic-but-informal register; it is not a substitute for ceremonial copy.

phrases.english_concept: engraving / inscribing a name on a gift or object
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in a use-case list where a styled name is a design source for something physical. Be honest about the boundary — this site produces copy-paste text, not an engraving file.
phrases.good_example: يمكن استخدام الاسم المنسّق كمرجع بصري قبل حفر ونقش الأسماء على الهدية.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages. Avoid نقش alone where the ornamental-pattern reading would confuse — and note it sits adjacent to زخرفة (AR-001), the gaming head term, so keep them apart.

phrases.native_phrase: الرموز الغريبة / رموز غريبة بدل الحروف
phrases.english_concept: mojibake — garbled/unreadable symbols shown instead of Arabic text
phrases.country_or_market: pan-Arab MSA (evidence from Levant/Egypt/Gulf-mixed general tech web)
phrases.register: neutral, non-technical; used by ordinary users and by the help articles written for them
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the FAQ/H2 wording on any Arabic troubleshooting section about copied text arriving broken (e.g. «لماذا تظهر رموز غريبة بدل النص بعد النسخ؟»). It supports, never replaces, the page's primary target (زخرفة / زخرفة اسماء). Pair it with مربعات (AR-012) rather than merging them — the two are different failures and Arabic users distinguish them: مربعات = the glyph is missing, رموز غريبة = the bytes were misread.
phrases.good_example: لماذا تظهر رموز غريبة بدل الحروف بعد النسخ واللصق؟
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in a title/H1 (it is a symptom phrase, not a demand term). Do not use it for the empty-square case — that is مربعات. Avoid in legal/accessibility copy where the precise term ترميز/UTF-8 is required.

phrases.english_concept: Arabic script breakage — letters render disconnected/segmented instead of joined (the script-specific diacritic/shaping failure)
phrases.country_or_market: pan-Arab MSA (evidence: Arabic developer Q&A, game-chat context)
phrases.register: neutral; used identically by non-technical users and by developers describing the bug
phrases.content_surface: faq heading, troubleshooting h2, body, tool warning copy
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in the Arabic troubleshooting FAQ that explains why an Arabic name may not survive decoration, and in any warning shown when Arabic input is styled. This is the single most locale-specific breakage phrase in the Arabic market — an Arabic page that only covers مربعات is answering a Latin-script market's problem in Arabic words.
phrases.good_example: لماذا تظهر الحروف مقطعة وغير متصلة داخل شات اللعبة؟
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use it for missing glyphs (مربعات) or for wrong-encoding garbling (الرموز الغريبة) — Arabic users treat all three as different problems. Not a title/H1 term.

phrases.usage_guidance: مزخرفة ("decorated") is the native decorative modifier and outdraws the literal جميلة ("beautiful") 8:1 — 880/mo vs 110/mo. The same modifier carries to إطارات مزخرفة (frames, 170) and فواصل مزخرفة (dividers, 30).
phrases.avoid_when: Not for technical/reference symbol pages (medical, currency, keyboard), which take plain رموز + the domain noun.
